faqs.question: What is a good short Halloween quote?
faqs.answer: Keep it to four or five words so it reads on a phone or a pumpkin sign: "Fog in, fun on" or "Pumpkins lit. Porch ready." The short list on this page has nine lines between four and five words.

faqs.question: Who said "Something wicked this way comes"?
faqs.answer: The Second Witch in Shakespeare's Macbeth, Act 4 Scene 1, written around 1606. The full couplet is "By the pricking of my thumbs, / Something wicked this way comes."

faqs.question: Did Robert Burns write a poem about Halloween?
faqs.answer: Yes. Burns wrote "Halloween" in 1785 and it was printed in 1786. It opens "Upon that night, when fairies light / On Cassilis Downans dance", and his own footnote calls it a night when witches and devils are abroad on their "baneful midnight errands".

faqs.question: What is the real Sleepy Hollow quote from the book?
faqs.answer: Washington Irving's 1820 story says "A drowsy, dreamy influence seems to hang over the land, and to pervade the very atmosphere." "Villainy wears many masks", often credited to Ichabod Crane, does not appear anywhere in Irving's text, so check the source before you print.

faqs.question: What did L. M. Montgomery say about October?
faqs.answer: In Anne of Green Gables (1908), chapter 16, Anne says "I'm so glad I live in a world where there are Octobers." The novel is in the public domain, so you can quote it with the title and year.

faqs.question: Can I put movie quotes from Hocus Pocus on a sign I sell?
faqs.answer: Be careful: Hocus Pocus came out in 1993 and is still under copyright, so short film lines on merchandise carry legal risk. Public-domain text such as Shakespeare, Burns or Irving, or a line you write yourself, avoids the problem.

faqs.question: Why do people like scary Halloween quotes?
faqs.answer: Rozin and colleagues (2013) call it benign masochism: enjoying a negative feeling in a safe setting. Thrill rides scored 56.5 out of 100 for liking in their sample of 390 people, and they found many prefer an experience just below the level they cannot tolerate.

faqs.question: Which Halloween quotes are OK for kids?
faqs.answer: Use the cute and short lists, such as "Little ghost, big hugs." Skip the creepy lines for young children, whose tolerance for fright is lower than an adult's, and avoid film lines with gore.

faqs.question: What is a motivational Halloween quote?
faqs.answer: Try "Courage is a costume until it fits" or "Brave isn't fearless. Brave is scared and still knocking." Lines with a mirrored shape, like "Don't let the fear wear you; wear the fear", tend to feel truer to readers, according to a 797-person chiasmus study.

faqs.question: When is Halloween?
faqs.answer: Halloween is on 31 October every year. It falls on a Saturday in 2026 and a Sunday in 2027, and All Saints' Day follows on 1 November.

# Halloween Quotes: 8 Sourced Classics and 82 Lines by Mood

The best Halloween quotes are short, sorted by mood, and either attributed exactly or written fresh. Below are 8 public-domain lines from Shakespeare to Lovecraft, each checked word for word against Project Gutenberg, plus 82 originals sorted by mood, including a 31-day "quote of the day" list. Across all SubhSandesh page types, 48.3% of shared pages are opened on a phone, so a quote gets one small screen, and each page averages 11.1 views, so the line gets reread. A table matches each mood to a use and a length.

## What makes a Halloween quote worth sharing?

A Halloween quote is a short line, attributed or original, that names the season's mix of fear and fun in a form people repeat. The ones that last are compact and patterned, like the *Macbeth* witches, still quoted after 400 years.

Two studies explain the pull. In [Rozin and colleagues' 2013 benign-masochism study](https://www.cambridge.org/core/journals/judgment-and-decision-making/article/glad-to-be-sad-and-other-examples-of-benign-masochism/48C0EC2F04412F3CB6EBC18B5E539BE8) (243 University of Pennsylvania students plus 147 online adults), thrill rides scored a mean liking of 56.5 out of 100. Many people, the authors conclude, like a negative experience "just below the level that cannot be tolerated": the target for a scary quote.

Form matters too. In [Kara-Yakoubian and colleagues' chiasmus experiments](https://osf.io/preprints/psyarxiv/c36q5) (N = 797), people judged reversed-order statements more accurate in three of four tests, and faster processing predicted the rating. Some inspirational lines below use that A-B-B-A shape.

## 8 public-domain Halloween quotes, with work and year

Each matches the Gutenberg edition named. Quote them as written and credit the work and year.

1. > "'Tis now the very witching time of night, / When churchyards yawn, and hell itself breathes out / Contagion to this world."

   William Shakespeare, *Hamlet*, Act 3 Scene 2 (c. 1600; Gutenberg eBook #1524).
2. > "By the pricking of my thumbs, / Something wicked this way comes."

   Shakespeare, *Macbeth*, Act 4 Scene 1 (c. 1606; eBook #1533).
3. > "Upon that night, when fairies light / On Cassilis Downans dance"

   Robert Burns, "Halloween", written 1785, printed 1786 ([Poems and Songs of Robert Burns](https://www.gutenberg.org/ebooks/1279)).
4. > "Is thought to be a night when witches, devils, and other mischief-making beings are abroad on their baneful midnight errands"

   Burns's own footnote to the poem.
5. > "A drowsy, dreamy influence seems to hang over the land, and to pervade the very atmosphere."

   Washington Irving, *[The Legend of Sleepy Hollow](https://www.gutenberg.org/ebooks/41)* (1820).
6. > "I'm so glad I live in a world where there are Octobers."

   L. M. Montgomery, *[Anne of Green Gables](https://www.gutenberg.org/ebooks/45)* (1908), chapter 16.
7. > "Listen to them—the children of the night. What music they make!"

   Bram Stoker, *Dracula* (1897), chapter 2 (eBook #345).
8. > "The most merciful thing in the world, I think, is the inability of the human mind to correlate all its contents."

   H. P. Lovecraft, "[The Call of Cthulhu](https://www.gutenberg.org/ebooks/68283)" (*Weird Tales*, 1928).

## 51 original Halloween quotes, sorted by mood

Written for this page and kept clean. Use them anywhere, no credit needed.

### Funny Halloween quotes (8)

- I'm not saying I'm a witch, but my coffee bubbles when I glare at it.
- My costume is "adult who bought the sweets early and ate half by the 30th".
- Ghosts have the easiest costume: one sheet, two holes, done.
- Calories don't count if the chocolate is shaped like a bat.
- I dressed as a vampire because I already avoid mornings.
- Take one sweet. The cat is watching. So am I.
- My haunted house is just my kitchen after the party.
- The scariest thing on the street is the dentist's diary on 1 November.

### Short Halloween quotes (9)

- Pumpkins lit. Porch ready.
- Boo, but make it cosy.
- Fog in, fun on.
- Sweets first, scares second.
- Darker nights, brighter grins.
- One night, every mask.
- Lanterns out, stories in.
- Spooky and not sorry.
- Small witch, big broom.

### Cute Halloween quotes (7)

- Little ghost, big hugs.
- Our pumpkin is smiling because you carved it.
- Tiny boots, giant puddles, best night.
- Even the bats fly home to someone.
- Best treat of the night: your gap-toothed grin.
- A pocket full of sweets and a heart full of giggles.
- The friendliest ghost on the street lives in our house.

### Scary and creepy Halloween quotes (7)

- The porch light flickered twice. Nobody was near the switch.
- Count the trick-or-treaters. Now count the footprints.
- The mask came off. The face underneath kept smiling.
- We carved the pumpkin last night. Today it is grinning wider.
- Fog doesn't hide things. It brings them closer.
- The last house on the street never runs out of sweets. Nobody lives there.
- Listen. The leaves are walking.

### Halloween quotes for adults and grown-ups (6)

- Grown-ups still dress up; we just call it "being fine".
- Adulthood is buying full-size bars and pretending they're for the neighbours.
- Halloween in my thirties: same costume, earlier bedtime.
- I no longer fear monsters. I fear the group chat choosing a costume theme.
- As kids we feared the dark. Now we pay to sit in it at the cinema.
- Tea in one hand, torch in the other: grown-up trick-or-treating.

### Inspirational and motivational Halloween quotes (7)

- Don't let the fear wear you; wear the fear.
- Courage is a costume until it fits.
- Brave isn't fearless. Brave is scared and still knocking.
- Carve out the fear and a light fits inside.
- Masks off, chin up.
- Face the night, and the night gets smaller.
- Hold the lantern up; the lantern holds you up.

### Halloween night and vibes quotes (7)

- Halloween night: where the streetlights lose to the pumpkins.
- Cold air, warm cider, every porch glowing orange.
- The moon is low, the bags are heavy, the night is ours.
- Leaf crunch, door knock, sweet wrapper, repeat.
- Vibe check: foggy, glowing and slightly haunted.
- Midnight on the 31st feels older than the clock says.
- October's last night wears its best black.

## 31 Halloween quotes of the day, 1 to 31 October

Halloween falls on 31 October every year. This list gives one line per date.

1. October opened the door. Something old walked in.
2. Thirty days to find your costume.
3. Light a candle for every story this month.
4. Gourds on the step are a promise.
5. The leaves fall like a rehearsed ghost story.
6. Wear one black thing; call it festive.
7. Every crow on the fence is counting down.
8. Buy the sweets. Hide the sweets. Repeat.
9. Jumpers by day, spooky films by night.
10. Ten days in, the porch looks haunted.
11. Fog is October whispering.
12. Pick a pumpkin with a face already in it.
13. The 13th has teeth, whatever the weekday.
14. Practise your "boo" on someone who'll laugh.
15. Halfway there, and the moon has noticed.
16. Old houses talk after dark.
17. Strong cocoa, stronger stories.
18. Read one ghost story aloud tonight.
19. Stitch, glue, repeat: costume season.
20. Eleven nights left. The bats said yes.
21. Carve slowly. Faces take patience.
22. Leave a light on for the wanderers.
23. One cobweb counts as decorating.
24. One week out: candles bought, nerves rising.
25. Choose the costume that makes you laugh.
26. Five nights left for the scary films.
27. Test the torch batteries now, not on the 31st.
28. The pumpkins are grinning at something behind you.
29. The bowl is full. Your willpower isn't.
30. Tomorrow the doors open. Tonight, the stories.
31. Knock, knock. It's finally here.

## Which Halloween quote fits where?

Each mood, where it works best, and the word range of this page's examples.

| Mood | Best use | Length | Example |
|---|---|---|---|
| Short | Pumpkin sign, Story sticker | 4–5 words | "Fog in, fun on." |
| Funny | Group chat, office card | 10–15 words | "Ghosts have the easiest costume: one sheet, two holes, done." |
| Scary | Party sign, adult post | 5–14 words | "Listen. The leaves are walking." |
| Classic (public domain) | Invitation, letter, framed print | 10–21 words | Burns, "Halloween", 1785 |
| Of the day | One post a day, 1–31 October | 4–9 words | "Fog is October whispering." |

The shorter the screen, the shorter the line; save 20-word classics for paper.

## Putting one Halloween quote on a page for one person

A quote in a group chat scrolls away. For the one person you want to surprise, the [interactive Halloween card](https://subhsandesh.in/happy-halloween) gives the line somewhere to live: they knock three times on a little haunted house, carve a jack-o'-lantern until your word glows, and read your letter by flashlight in a dark attic. Put the Montgomery "Octobers" line in that letter and add up to six photos.

It has partner, bestie, family and kids modes; the kids tone has no gore and no jump scares, so keep the creepy list for adults. It ends with a 1080×1920 Boo License. If you want to read the quote aloud, the [cinematic Halloween page](https://subhsandesh.in/happy-halloween-premium) adds a voice note of up to 60 seconds, up to 12 photos and a 3,000-character letter. And 90.9% of started SubhSandesh pages get published and shared.

## When a Halloween quote is the wrong choice

Neither template is a party tool: both are one-person greeting pages, English only. For a crowd or a shop window, print the quote.

Scary lines suit adults. Rozin's "just below the intolerable" was measured in adults, and a five-year-old's limit sits far lower. Film lines are another trap: *Hocus Pocus* (1993) is still under copyright, so use public-domain text or your own words. And 1 November is All Saints' Day, with Día de los Muertos on 1–2 November, so for anyone recently bereaved a jokey skeleton line can land badly.

## Sources

[Glad to be sad, and other examples of benign masochism](https://www.cambridge.org/core/journals/judgment-and-decision-making/article/glad-to-be-sad-and-other-examples-of-benign-masochism/48C0EC2F04412F3CB6EBC18B5E539BE8). *Judgment and Decision Making* 8(4): 439–447.

structuralLimitations: Contested head term: the measured Google SERP (serps.md) has 2/10 weak results (today, southern living, rd, T+L, shutterfly, bouqs, chatbooks); the WebSearch re-check this run (US-served index, NOT Google's ranking, lower confidence; Firecrawl disconnected) returned romper, scarymommy, rd, today, educatorstechnology (2024), purewow x2, getcompass (off-intent sales), romper — about 2 weak. Gate 4 passes (non-zero weak) but win probability is low; long-tail alternatives: 'halloween quotes of the day for october', 'public domain halloween quotes with source', 'short halloween quotes for pumpkin signs'.
No Halloween usage data exists in facts.md; all three first-party lines are platform-wide and the body labels the phone figure as all page types.
Kara-Yakoubian et al.: only the PsyArXiv abstract was read; the 2022 Canadian Journal of Experimental Psychology version (APA) is paywalled. The body cites only what the abstract states.

Hamlet, Macbeth and Dracula were verified against Gutenberg eBooks #1524, #1533 and #345 but are cited by eBook number in the body, not linked, to stay inside the 3–6 outbound-link rule.
